title: Reference-based eval normalization and signal attribution pilot
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Objective: Reduce noisy alerts and improve root-cause attribution for quality regressions that follow model/config rollouts. We'll introduce a reference-based normalization layer (per-model, per-config baselines) and an attribution pipeline that quantifies how much a change in model/config explains observed metric drift. This will combine LLM-as-judge judgments (calibrated) with statistical baselines to make regression signals actionable.

Why now: Current regression alerts are high-noise when we change tokenization, sampling temperature, or quantization profile. Engineers spend time chasing false positives. A reference-normalization approach plus signal attribution should lower alert volume and speed up mitigation.

High-level approach:
- Build a reference baseline store keyed by model-version, config-hash, and workload bucket (prompt archetypes). Baselines store median and variance for key eval metrics.
- When a rollout occurs, compute per-batch delta relative to matched baseline using paired sampling where possible.
- Run LLM-as-judge on a stratified sample to provide semantic scoring and pairwise preference labels; apply calibration layer to align judge confidence with human labels.
- Combine statistical deltas with judge signals into a single attribution score and surface the top probable causes (model weight change, sampling, quantization, prompt edits).

Deliverables:
- Baseline store and normalization pipeline
- Judge calibration routine + calibration artifact storage
- Attribution scoring service + explanation metadata for Console
- New Grafana dashboard and alerting rules with adjusted thresholds
- Runbook for interpreting attribution outputs and suggested mitigations

Non-goals: This pilot does not attempt to replace full human evaluation for high-impact regressions; nor to automate rollbacks without human sign-off.
tasks: Implement paired-sample ingestion from production eval streams (ENG-4413)
Design attribution scoring heuristics and thresholds (PM & ENG)
Design Console panels and drilldowns for attribution (DES-321)
Create alerting rules and initial threshold recommendations (PM)
Pilot with two internal teams and collect feedback (PM-9321)
Prepare runbook and training session for SRE/SEs
success_metrics: Reduce regression alert false positives by >= 40% in pilot workloads
Median time-to-triage for regressions reduced from 3h to <90m
Attribution precision: top-1 predicted cause matches human investigation >= 70%
Judge calibration: model confidence calibration error < 0.08 (ECE) on held-out manual labels
risks: LLM-judge drift over time causing systematic misattribution
Insufficient matched baseline data for low-volume prompt archetypes
Increased pipeline latency for eval processing could slow alerting
Human label cost for calibration may be higher than estimated
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design and data collection (2 weeks) - collect matched pairs and define archetypes
Phase 1: Internal pilot (2 weeks) - run on two product teams with parallel existing alerts
Phase 2: Iterate thresholds and calibration (1 week) - tune using human labels
Phase 3: Wider beta (3 teams, 4 weeks) - add Console surfaces and alerting
Phase 4: GA and docs (post-pilot) - publish runbook, tooling, and onboarding guide
